purpose: Reject contradictory source/odometry/calibration/volume identities and totals in portable full-bag mapping receipts. Validation correctness with synthetic states only; no physical accuracy or synchronization qualification.

fixed_contract.completed_source: A completed source must retain exactly one nonempty scan per selected physical message, matching the existing full-bag producer admission. Require each topic's message/record counts to agree, total points at least total records and both corrected timestamp bounds. Existing checked total arithmetic, ordered bounds, nonzero storage and truncation rules remain. Partial source receipts may retain a prefix and remain valid blocked diagnostics.
fixed_contract.odometry_binding: Every present odometry stage must name the selected front topic and cannot contain more scans than retained front records. A complete front trajectory must cover exactly the front records and front bag messages. Do not require rear completion for an otherwise complete front trajectory in a blocked diagnostic receipt. Existing graph connectivity/count arithmetic remains.
fixed_contract.identity_binding: When calibration is present, bind odometry's source frame to the registered front role, root frame to the calibration root and corrected clock ID to the target domain. Bind TSDF's frame to that root and, when odometry exists, to its root. The human-readable clock_domain label is not a typed clock identity; do not hardcode a label or claim extra measured timing evidence.
fixed_contract.coverage: TSDF totals count integration visits, not unique physical messages or unique retained points. Reused nearest rear records may increase visits beyond source totals, while unmatched records may reduce them. Preserve valid positive visit totals on either side of source totals; do not impose equality, a producer-specific upper bound, new matching semantics or a physical coverage claim. Partial finished-stage diagnostics remain permitted; full admission still requires every existing readiness flag and no blockers.
fixed_contract.compatibility: Keep schema version 1, serialized fields, public signatures and dependencies unchanged. Tighten explicit validate() and try_new() admission of contradictory states. Serde decoding still requires explicit validate(); test deserialize-then-validate, round trips and constructor rejection. Preserve healthy completed states, blocked missing-calibration states and consistent partial prefixes.
fixed_contract.scope: Safe immutable validation in spatialrust-viewer only. Preserve production source/clock/frame registration, full-bag producer, matching, collection budgets, transport, odometry, TSDF computation, core/GPU/Python and explicit device ownership. No hidden copies, new threads, dependency or artificial calibration.

verification: Commit this protocol first. Reuse the existing complete synthetic fixture as a test helper without changing its values. Run regression tests against unchanged parent validators, retain actual behavioral failures, then implement immutable cross-stage checks. Cover source cardinality/points/bounds, complete/partial front counts and topic, calibration frame/root/clock, volume root, forged decoded receipts, constructor rejection, checked overflow, valid partial diagnostics, arbitrary descriptive clock labels and visit-versus-unique coverage. Run viewer default/serde/all-features, full-bag/E2E, ROS2/records/sync/mapping/calibration controls, viewer and ROS2 all-target Clippy, format. Reuse existing three-OS jobs and the full 131-check merge gate.

resources.preservation: Hash-protect all prior scientific JSON, 42 frozen native artifacts, pinned sources and completed room outputs. Reuse the cache and preserve failed logs. No real sensor read/download/copy, real-motion fit or frozen build. Any synthetic temporary data stays in the owned external root.

remaining_80_percent: Native full-room accuracy and genuinely unobserved motion; both qualifying raw Linux hardware classes; matching canonical measured clock uncertainty and physical frame accuracy; complete canonical mapping/semantic/Viewer/interchange/release acceptance. Portable receipt consistency does not establish these requirements or unique fusion coverage.
